statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt under 90 minutes before the 22:00Z reopen, against Stress of 69% (high) while the Strait of Hormuz stays closed on Iran's seven stated conditions and fresh Sunday incidents were reported in the strait and off Yemen.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail holds its halt-session floor under 90 minutes before the 22:00Z CME reopen as Sunday strait incidents lift Stress to 69%
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so under 90 minutes before the reopen no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly and two-way: the cash index set a record intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, surrendered it in full, and closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.60 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. December NQ futures settled at 31,049, up 0.94%, which is the reference for any weekend gap. A record close that gives back its own high is the opposite of the no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure.

Stress rises one point to 69% because the weekend headline stack kept building while the market could not price it. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf repeated that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi paired diplomacy with a warning of military preparedness. Monitoring recorded a single transit on 27 September against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 a day, with 218 AIS-visible vessels holding position away from working ports. During Sunday, explosions were reported in the strait and a tanker reported multiple explosions about 60 nautical miles south of Al Mukha, Yemen, while Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned with NIOC chief executive Hamid Bovard named acting minister.

Cross-assets conflict rather than align, which under this contract raises Stress and uncertainty instead of Tail. September payrolls rose 29,000 against roughly a 90,000 consensus and unemployment edged to 4.2%, leaving October Fed hold odds near 77%, yet the 2-year yield still ended Friday up at 4.837% and the 10-year at 5.279% after an initial fall. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31, near its session low, while WTI eased 1.90% to $91.11 and Brent sat near $102.25 after the G7 agreed to deploy 100 million barrels of reserves over four months. Low volatility and softer crude alongside a shut strait is conflict, not the aligned amplifier stack Tail requires.

The published forecast therefore keeps every hour in EA_ON except the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, where Tail is raised to 22% and 20% inside the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity grounds. That step is conditional on an untested reopen, not on observed one-way structure, and an early genuine retracement would invalidate it. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September with a partial collection status, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used as evidence; this assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green and the dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting a market that was either in orderly two-way trade or closed. Stress rose from 67% at 20:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend Hormuz checkpoints opened, then eased through the 73%, 70%, 68% and 66% readings of the European and US-equivalent hours to settle in a 64% to 68% band. Confidence ran between 83% and 88%, improving through the Sunday hours as current levels, yields, oil and the forward calendar were re-verified while the live price path stayed structurally unavailable inside the weekend halt.
outlookSummary: The current closed hour carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held at 3% while Stress sits at 69% on the closed strait and the Sunday incident flow. Tail steps to 8% in the final closed hour and is raised to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which the published danger window covers; that step reflects weekend-gap and thin-liquidity hazard rather than observed one-way structure, and an early orderly retracement would invalidate it. Tail then decays to a 7% to 9% range through the Asian and European sessions, rebuilds to 10% and 11% into the US pre-market, reaches 15% at the 13:30Z cash open, peaks at 17% for the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, and eases back to 11% by the final published hour. Stress trends down from 72% at the reopen to 61% by the end of the horizon, and every forecast hour outside the two reopen slots maps to EA_ON and green.

forecastDetail.comment: No Nasdaq-100 price path is observable inside the CME weekend halt, so Tail holds its 3% floor while Stress sits at 69% on the closed Strait of Hormuz and the weekend incidents reported in and around it.

The last closed hour before the 22:00Z reopen lifts Tail only to 8% for positioning uncertainty; no price can print, so no structure is scoreable, and Stress rises to 70% on the building weekend headline stack.

The 22:00Z CME reopen carries weekend-gap and thin-liquidity hazard, which places forecast Tail at 22% in the WATCH band against the 31,049 December NQ settlement reference rather than against any observed one-way move.
Tail stays at 20% in the WATCH band while a reopen gap is absorbed; an early genuine retracement would invalidate the step and return the path to single digits.
Tail eases to 12% on the conditional assumption that the gap has been absorbed into the Asian handover, with Stress at 68% while the strait stays shut and oil prices no fresh escalation.
The Asian session is modelled back at a 9% quiet-session Tail provided no one-way structure carried over from the reopen, with Stress easing to 66%.
